summary.title: Night noise from upstairs neighbours
summary.what_happened: My upstairs neighbours have a newborn who cries at night. On weekends they play loud music until about 2am. I have banged on the ceiling with a broom a few times. I have not spoken to them directly. The building rules set quiet hours from 22:00 to 07:00.
summary.my_feelings: I feel exhausted and worn down. I work early shifts and the noise is costing me sleep.
summary.my_needs: I need to sleep at night so I can work my early shifts.
summary.desired_outcome: I want the loud music and the crying to stop at night.

consult.text:
It makes sense that you are exhausted. Early shifts are hard enough without broken sleep, and weekend music until 2am would wear anyone down.

Your neighbours may see this differently. With a newborn, they are probably very tired too. They may not know the sound carries to you, and they may not realise you are bothered, because you have not spoken to them. A baby's crying is not something parents can switch off.

One thing that may have made this harder is the broom. Banging on the ceiling can feel hostile to someone who has never heard a word from you. It may also have made them defensive. The music is different. Music until 2am breaks the quiet hours you mentioned, and that is a fair complaint.

What we do not know is whether they are aware of the problem at all, or whether the crying is every night or only sometimes.

Some steps to consider:
1. Talk to them in person or leave a friendly note. Start with the music, since that is something they can change.
2. Ask if there is anything that would help with the crying, such as a rug, and share your work hours.
3. If the music continues after that, contact the landlord, pointing to the quiet hours rule.
Babies crying is still noise. Why should I put up with it just because it's a baby?

You do not have to love the crying, and it is fair to be tired and frustrated by it. I am not saying you should simply put up with it. Newborn crying is just hard to control, and most people treat it differently from music, because the parents cannot choose to stop it. That is why I would keep the two things apart.

The music is a clear request. It goes past the quiet hours, and they can stop it. The crying is more a matter of living in a shared building. Some things might help, like asking if a rug or moving the crib away from the floor could soften the sound, or you could try earplugs or white noise on your side.

I also still think speaking to them first matters. They have not heard from you except through the broom. A calm word may get you further than a complaint to the landlord, who can then be the next step if nothing changes.

Would you like help writing a short, friendly message to them?

share_draft: Hi, I live in the flat below you. I wanted to talk to you directly, and I am sorry I banged on the ceiling a few times instead of coming to speak with you. I work early shifts, and I am struggling to get enough sleep at the moment. I know you have a newborn, and I understand that crying is hard to avoid. The loud music on weekends until about 2am is what is hardest for me, since the building quiet hours are 22:00 to 07:00. Could we find a way to keep the nights quieter? I would really like to hear how things look from your side, too.
harsh_draft: Some of us have jobs. Control your kid and turn off your music or I'm calling the landlord.
